Step-by-Step Audio Guided Tour: Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, Newton MA - Walking Tour
Tour-Category: walking

Stop 1: Nave

Address: 321 Washington Street, Newton, MA 02465

Coordinates: 42.3376, -71.2075

Type/Specialty: Main worship area

Specific Examples: Beautiful stained glass windows, wooden pews, altar decorations

Orientation: You are about to embark on a walking journey through Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, Newton MA. The church stands as a testament to the enduring faith of its congregants. Explore how this church has evolved to play a pivotal role in the neighborhood, weaving together tales of the past with the present congregation's steadfast beliefs. As you continue on the tour, you will learn about Father Cuenin's public criticism of Cardinal Bernard Law and the Archdiocese of Boston at the Ambo and the parish's Finance Council's skepticism regarding financial improprieties at the Chancel. Your first stop is Nave. From the Newton Centre T station, head southeast on Washington Street for about 0.5 miles. The church will be on your left. As you walk, notice the charming local shops lining the street. Stand near the entrance of the nave, where the light streams through the intricately designed stained glass windows. As you look up, let your gaze follow the elegant arches that sweep across the ceiling, drawing your attention to the vastness of the space.

As you stand here in the nave of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, Massachusetts, you're in a place that has borne witness to pivotal events in the church's recent history. One such moment occurred in December 2002, when Rev. Walter H. Cuenin took a bold stand against Cardinal Bernard Law. In response to the Cardinal's fundraising efforts amidst a brewing scandal, Father Cuenin organized an archdiocesan priests' meeting right here in this nave. This act was not just a gathering but a statement, leading to Cardinal Law banning all official archdiocesan activities from this church. The consequence of this defiance was profound, marking a significant moment of tension between local clergy and the archdiocesan leadership. Just days later, on December 8, 2002, over 850 parishioners filled this very nave. They came together to support Father Cuenin, who delivered a poignant homily against Cardinal Law. The scene was one of unity and resolve, as the congregation rose to give Father Cuenin multiple standing ovations. This powerful demonstration of support contributed to a larger movement within the church, as Rev. Cuenin, along with 58 other priests, spearheaded an open letter demanding Cardinal Law's resignation. The impact was swift and decisive—Cardinal Law resigned days after the letter was released. The nave has also been a place of solace and community in times of tragedy. On June 25, 2023, the church held a Mass of Peace and vigil in memory of Bruno and Gilda D’Amore, who were tragically murdered in their home. On June 25, 2023, seventy-three-year-old Gilda D’Amore was killed alongside her husband, Bruno D’Amore, and her ninety-seven-year-old mother, Lucia Arpino, after suffering blunt force trauma and multiple stab wounds during a home break-in on Broadway Street in Newton, Massachusetts. Forty-one-year-old Christopher Ferguson was arrested and charged with their murders, burglary, and assault. Hundreds gathered to mourn and find comfort here, demonstrating the nave's role as a sanctuary for the community in their time of need. As you take in the beauty of the stained glass and the architectural grandeur, remember the stories of courage, unity, and solace that have unfolded within these walls.

Directions: As you exit the Nave of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, head towards the main entrance on Washington Street. Walk straight ahead to reach the beautiful Portico at the front of the church. You can't miss the impressive columns and intricate architectural details that mark the entrance.

Stop 2: Portico

Address: 321 Washington Street, Newton, MA 02465

Coordinates: 42.3372, -71.2094

Type/Specialty: Entrance area

Specific Examples: Columns with intricate designs, welcoming space for gatherings, views of the church grounds

Orientation: As you exit the nave you stopped at a moment ago, pause at the entrance to the Portico to appreciate its architectural details.

The Portico of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, Massachusetts, invites you to consider its role not just as an architectural feature, but as a historical witness to the life and events of the parish. Cuenin, then the parish priest, courageously spoke out against Cardinal Bernard Law, the archbishop of boston from 1984, criticizing his handling of the crisis. However, Father Cuenin's actions resonated deeply with the community. In a remarkable show of support, more than 850 parishioners gathered at the church, giving Father Cuenin standing ovations and embracing him as a sign of solidarity. 1995, Mother Teresa made an unexpected visit to the church, drawing spontaneous crowds eager to see or receive a blessing from the revered humanitarian. Her presence not only brought the community together but also highlighted the church's significance as a gathering place for moments of both joy and contemplation.

Directions: As you exit the Portico, walk straight ahead towards the main entrance of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church. Continue through the nave, past the altar, and you'll reach the Chancel area where you can admire the beautiful stained glass windows. Enjoy your stroll through this historic church in Newton, MA!

Stop 3: Chancel

Address: 321 Washington Street, Newton, MA 02465

Coordinates: 42.3372, -71.2062

Type/Specialty: Liturgical area behind the altar

Specific Examples: Decorative altar, choir area, religious artifacts

Orientation: As you stand before the Chancel, notice the way the light from the stained glass windows dances across the altar, casting a spectrum of colors that seem to breathe life into this sacred space. This is the heart of Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church in Newton, MA, where the spiritual and historical converge.

The Chancel holds a special significance in the life of the church, not only as a space for liturgical functions but as a witness to pivotal episodes in the community's history. One such moment occurred in September 2005 when Father Walter H. Cuenin announced his resignation from his position here. The Archdiocese had accused him of financial improprieties, a charge that was met with skepticism by the parish's own Finance Council. This episode sent ripples through the community, highlighting the complex relationship between the parish and the Archdiocese, and sparking discussions about transparency and trust in church governance. Neighbor Christopher Ferguson was arrested and charged with their murders after investigators connected him to the scene through bloody footprints, fingerprints, and DNA. This tragedy struck at the core of the community, leading to a deeply emotional memorial service and a Mass of Peace held within these walls. The event underscored the Chancel’s role not only as a place of celebration but also as a sanctuary for mourning and healing. As you reflect upon these stories, consider the Chancel not just as an architectural feature but as a living narrative of the parish's trials and triumphs. Beyond this space, the Ambo awaits, holding yet another chapter in the church's storied history.

Directions: As you stand at the Chancel in Our Lady Help of Christians Catholic Church, walk towards the front of the church. Head past the altar and continue straight towards the elevated platform known as the Ambo. You'll pass the lectern on your way.

Stop 4: Ambo

Address: 321 Washington Street, Newton, MA 02465

Coordinates: 42.3374, -71.2082

Type/Specialty: Pulpit for readings

Specific Examples: Artistic design, central location for scripture readings, often adorned with flowers

Orientation: As you enter the next stop on our tour, take a moment to focus on the Ambo, a central piece of ecclesiastical furniture that is often overlooked. Positioned prominently in the chancel area you visited earlier, the Ambo stands as a focal point for sermons and readings, its presence both commanding and inviting.

 Father Cuenin used his pulpit to openly criticize Cardinal Bernard Law and the Archdiocese of Boston, addressing issues that had shaken the community. His bold stance earned him two standing ovations from a congregation of over 850 parishioners. This moment underscored the church's role as a platform for social justice and activism, significantly impacting both the local community and the broader Catholic Church. The Ambo has also been a stage for dramatic and unexpected turns. Allegations of financial improprieties leveled by the Archdiocese of Boston led to his sudden departure. This event left the parish in a turbulent state, highlighting the Ambo's role as not just a place for spiritual guidance but also for communal reflection and challenge. The Ambo, a modest yet significant fixture, has thus borne witness to both triumph and tribulation. Its stories are woven into the fabric of the church's history and its evolving mission. In a larger context, the Catholic Church, which includes an estimated 1.28 to 1.41 billion baptized members worldwide as of 2026, has been a cornerstone in addressing social issues and spiritual guidance. As you contemplate these narratives, consider how the Ambo’s role in this church mirrors the evolving role of Catholicism itself.

That's 4 stops — Chancel accused of financial improprieties by Archdiocese, doubted by parish council and Nave Father Cuenin organized priests' meeting in response to Cardinal's fundraising. If you would like to eat nearby we can build you a restaurant tour.
